codeReview.summary: The feature improves stale-heartbeat handling and runtime status repair, but the new supervisor status path can cancel its own scheduled recovery on the very next status poll.

issues.description: When `get_stream_status()` sees a running/starting stream transition to `STOPPED`/`EXITED`, it schedules an auto-restart by flipping the record to `error`. But a later status poll against the same still-stopped supervisor program takes the `previous_status == "error"` branch at lines 628-664, rewrites the stream to `stopped`, and leaves `runtime_next_restart_at` populated. `restart_due_streams()` only dispatches rows where `Stream.status == "error"` (`backend/app/core/stream_reconciler.py:526-527`), so the queued recovery is silently orphaned and the stream never restarts. This is user-reachable because the streaming UI polls `/api/streams/{id}/status` every 5s for error streams (`frontend/src/app/dashboard/streaming/page.tsx:110`).

summary: Fail: repeated supervisor status reads can downgrade an auto-restart candidate from `error` to `stopped`, which removes it from the restart dispatcher query and breaks the promised recoverable post-failure state.
